transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Avery (Nexara ML Platform), Devon (Nexara Eng Dir), Samir (Nexara Data Scientist)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Quant pilot results: INT8 brings ~1.8x throughput, median token latency down ~24-28% on test harness; FP8 shows similar perf but slightly higher variability.
- Quality: measured SNR-style metric (signal-to-noise on NER/slot extraction) shows a 0.6-1.2 pts delta on highest priority prompts; perceptible in edge-cases.
- Tuning: recommend per-channel calibration + small learning-rate-aware bias correction and targeted retriggers on top-k attention layers.
- Next steps: per-channel sweep, expanded 5k eval set, schedule production-like latency run on dedicated pool.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): all right hey everyone thanks for joining, we've got about 40 minutes, we'll run through last week's bench results, dig into the quality deltas and agree next steps.
[00:18] Avery (Nexara): yep, thanks Maya. Quick scheduling note, Devon will need to drop at 15:30, so probably want to get the ops ask before then.
[00:26] Maya: noted. Carlos will lead the perf segment, I'll cover pricing and pilot logistics.

[02:05] Carlos (Redwood): okay so quick recap of the harness runs — we used your 1k production-like prompts, batch size 8 for throughput sim, and the dedicated-edge config. INT8 quant gave us a steady 1.8x throughput increase, median token latency reduced from 45ms to ~33ms, p95 moved from 120ms to 95ms on the test box. FP8 was roughly comparable in mean but p95 spikier, we saw some 180-200ms tails on a few long-sequence examples.
[02:40] Samir (Nexara): hmm the tails are worrying for our chat UX; do you have traces of the outliers?
[02:44] Carlos: yes, we captured traces — main noise seems to be KV-cache misses and one attention kernel falling back to a slower path on one CUDA kernel. I'll share the log bundle.

[05:12] Devon (Nexara): on quality, Samir ran the slot-fill tests overnight — what's the delta look like? We care about false positives on entity extraction.
[05:21] Samir: right, short answer: for most prompts precision held, but recall dropped on nested entities and long context windows. We computed a signal-to-noise-ish metric (we call it SNR here) — baseline FP32 SNR = 18.9, INT8 SNR = 18.1, FP8 SNR = 17.8 on the initial 1k set. So roughly a 0.8–1.1 decrease.
[05:52] Maya: good to hear the numbers, the delta is measurable but not catastrophic. Question is: are those deltas concentrated on a subset of prompts or uniformly distributed?
[06:04] Samir: concentrated — mostly long narratives and some low-occurrence medical entity tokens.

[08:20] Carlos: that fits hypothesis — quantization noise disproportionately affects rare token embeddings and high-attention layers. Two mitigations: per-channel quantization + bias correction, or selective float-fallback for top-K layers. Per-channel gave us back ~0.4 SNR points in our internal sweep.
[08:42] Avery: can you explain per-channel in simple terms? Our infra team is not deep into quant internals.
[08:47] Carlos: sure — instead of one scale for an entire weight matrix we compute a scaling factor per output channel. that reduces rounding noise for channels with different distributions. It costs slightly more memory for scales but keeps compute fast.

[11:10] Maya: small product/ops ask — if we recommend per-channel, how much operational complexity? Avery, will that be okay for your infra?
[11:20] Avery: we can take it, but we need a clear runbook and logs. We only want changes that are reversible quickly.
[11:27] Maya: absolutely, we'll supply a rollback toggle.

[13:02] Carlos: back to perf-quality tradeoffs — selective layer float-fallback (keep first 2 attention layers in FP16) recovered ~0.6 SNR on some patterns but reduced throughput gain to ~1.5x. So it's a tradeoff.
[13:30] Devon: tradeoff is expected; business question — is there a way to do targeted fallback only for prompts labeled high-risk?
[13:37] Carlos: yes, we can route by prompt classifier. Redwood Optimize can tag prompts and route to mixed-precision path for those that require higher fidelity. Latency will be higher only for that subset.

[15:05] Devon: I'm about to head out in 15 — quick ask: what would be the minimal change to push to a canary with low risk?
[15:12] Maya: minimal = per-channel INT8 with a canary traffic slice (5%) plus real-time regression guardrails. Carlos can run a short calibration and we deploy with auto-fallback to FP32 if quality drift crosses threshold.

[17:30] Samir: on evaluations — current set is 1k prompts, many short. We'll add 5k longer prompts with biz-priority labels as Avery mentioned. That should surface edge-case regressions.
[17:45] Avery: yes we'll upload the set by end of week.

[19:10] Carlos: technical note — we found one kernel in the test harness that falls back because of an indexing pattern; we can patch it in the runtime but it's a low-level kernel change and needs more verification. For now, per-channel avoids that fallback in most cases.
[19:36] Samir: can you quantify the patch risk? We prefer configuration changes over runtime patches.
[19:42] Carlos: patch risk is moderate — it's GPU-kernel work, we need regression tests. So prefer per-channel + small layer fallback as config first.

[22:00] Maya: pricing and pilot logistics — the dedicated pilot add-on for calibration runs will add a short usage bump; I'll send an updated pilot quote. Also our observability retention (token-level traces) is available as an add-on if you want longer retention for debugging.
[22:20] Avery: we'll want that during the pilot window, at least 30 days.

[24:40] Carlos: quick perf numbers to anchor things — baseline FP32 throughput: 250 reqs/s (batch 8). INT8 per-channel: 450 reqs/s. FP8: 420 reqs/s but with 8% tail variance. Latency medians as mentioned earlier. Quality: exact-match NER recall drop ~1.9% overall, concentrated in the 5% of prompts we flagged as long-context.
[25:10] Samir: exact-match recall is concerning only for those flagged prompts, for others it's within noise.

[27:05] Devon: what's the expected ROI if we go to INT8 per-channel vs keeping FP32? We need cost numbers for our finance team.
[27:12] Maya: rough math: compute cost reduction ~45-50% on serving, so if your inference spend is X, you could see ~0.45X reduction on token compute. We'll provide a model-level estimate based on your usage shape.

[30:00] Carlos: additional note — we recommend running an A/B in Dedicated for 60 minutes with representative traffic to validate p95 tails and end-to-end UX. We'll instrument traces and a quick feedback loop to rollback.
[30:17] Avery: agree. Can Redwood run that or do we need to provision?
[30:22] Carlos: Redwood can run it in your dedicated pilot pool; will coordinate with your infra to ensure endpoints and keys.

[32:45] Samir: one more quality experiment idea — small bias-correction fine-tune on a tiny subset of high-priority prompts (100-200 examples) for 1-2 epochs. In prior work that recovers ~0.3–0.6 SNR points with minimal cost.
[33:00] Carlos: yes lightweight fine-tune or LoRA style adapter is an option; we can include that as a follow-up if per-channel alone doesn't hit target.

[35:00] Devon: summarizing priorities before I go: 1) run per-channel calibration sweep, 2) expand eval prompts to 5k and label by biz-priority, 3) schedule 60-minute dedicated run, 4) get an updated pricing addendum.
[35:20] Maya: that's correct — action owners to confirm in notes.

[37:40] Carlos: I'll start the calibration sweep today and share logs; note: logs include kernel traces and quant scales — might have unintelligible fields but we'll annotate.
[38:10] Avery: thanks, also please include the rollback steps in the runbook so our SREs can revert in <10 minutes.
[38:20] Maya: will do.

[40:00] Maya: ok last quick QA — any other compliance or security blockers we should surface?
[40:08] Avery: SOC2 docs looked fine, we'll still want the on-prem checklist if we escalate to Private. For now pilot in Dedicated is fine.
[40:20] Maya: noted. We'll attach the SOC2 and the private deployment checklist to the follow-up email.

[41:00] Devon: I'm stepping off, thanks everyone.
[41:05] Maya: thanks Devon. Closing notes: we'll capture action items and send updated pricing and runbook by Friday.

Meeting end.
